theme: 3 terms on protocols that do more: adding shared methods to a protocol, giving requirements a fallback body, and leaving a type for each conformer to choose

terms.definition: An extension that adds methods or computed properties to every type that adopts a protocol.
terms.example: I added a protocol extension on `Greeter`, so all our greeting types get `greet()` for free.

terms.definition: A method body in a protocol extension that a conforming type uses when it does not write its own.
terms.example: `Square` doesn't write `describe()`, so it falls back to the default implementation.

terms.definition: A placeholder type name inside a protocol that each conforming type fills in with a real type.
terms.example: The protocol uses an associated type for `Item`, so each box decides what it stores.

quizzes.question: What do you call a placeholder type inside a protocol that each conforming type fills in?
What does a conforming type use when it skips writing a required method itself?
What lets you add one new method to all conforming types in a single place?

Learn to talk about protocols that do more than list rules: Protocol Extension, Default Implementation & Associated Type, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Protocol Extension - An extension that adds methods or computed properties to every type that adopts a protocol.
Default Implementation - A method body in a protocol extension that a conforming type uses when it does not write its own.
Associated Type - A placeholder type name inside a protocol that each conforming type fills in with a real type.

한국어: 연관 타입: 프로토콜 안의 자리표시자 타입 이름으로, 채택한 타입이 실제 타입을 정해요

landscape.hook: Can you explain these protocol terms in English?

dialogue.title: A method nobody wrote

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, `News` compiles, but I never wrote `title`. Why does it work?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The protocol extension on `Feed` gives `title` a default implementation.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, so every type that adopts `Feed` gets `title` for free?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. That's why a protocol extension is great for shared code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Can `News` replace the default implementation with its own?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Just write your own `title` inside `News`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. And what's `Item`? I thought protocols couldn't have generics.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's an associated type. Each conforming type decides what `Item` really is.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So I have to add `typealias Item = Int` inside `News`?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No need. Swift infers the associated type from `items`.
Write it once in a protocol extension, and every conformer gets it.
